classification.difficultyReason: Generalise the supplied small cases by separating corners, edges, face interiors and the cube interior, excluding boundaries to avoid double counting.

content.prompt: If a painted wooden cube is cut in half along each edge (making 8 smaller cubes), then each of these cubes is painted on three faces. If a painted wooden cube is cut into thirds along each edge (making 27 smaller cubes), 8 of these cubes are painted on three faces, 12 of these cubes are painted on two faces, 6 are painted on one face only, and one is not painted at all. If a painted wooden cube is cut into four parts along each edge, how many smaller cubes are there, and how many are painted on three, two, one and no faces, respectively? Find an expression for how many cubes are painted on three, two, one and no faces if the large cube is cut into $n$ parts along each edge.

answer.short:
64 smaller cubes; painted on three, two, one and no faces, respectively: $8,24,24,8$.

For integer $n\geq2$, the corresponding counts are $8$, $12(n-2)$, $6(n-2)^2$ and $(n-2)^3$.

Count corner cubes, edge cubes excluding corners, face-interior cubes and interior cubes separately.
answer.worked:
For integer $n\geq2$, there are $n$ smaller cubes along each edge, so there are $n^3$ smaller cubes altogether.

Three painted faces: only the 8 corner cubes have three painted faces.

Two painted faces: each of the 12 edges contains $n-2$ cubes after its two corner cubes are excluded. The count is $12(n-2)$.

One painted face: each of the 6 faces contains an interior square of $(n-2)\times(n-2)$ cubes. The count is $6(n-2)^2$.

No painted faces: removing the outside layer leaves an interior cube with $n-2$ cubes along each edge. The count is $(n-2)^3$.

For $n=4$:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Total}&=4^3\\\text{Total}&=64\\\text{Three faces}&=8\\\text{Two faces}&=12(4-2)\\\text{Two faces}&=24\\\text{One face}&=6(4-2)^2\\\text{One face}&=24\\\text{No faces}&=(4-2)^3\\\text{No faces}&=8\end{align*}$$
Check: $8+24+24+8=64$.
